headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks between Flowise and Gemini CLI.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and uploaded files, while Gemini CLI reads/writes repo files and user-provided directories and can use MCP. If Flowise outputs are placed in a shared workspace, Gemini CLI may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF Flowise writes agent outputs into a directory Gemini CLI reads
IF Gemini CLI parses those files as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Use separate directories for Flowise and Gemini CLI outputs
Disable automatic ingestion of Flowise-generated files into Gemini CLI prompts
Add a manual review step before Gemini CLI consumes any Flowise artifact
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate containers or workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem access, and both touch files in shared workspaces by default. Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and tool credentials; Gemini CLI handles source code, cwd files, and shell environment. That creates a plausible path for sensitive data to flow from one agent’s workspace into the other’s outputs or API calls.
conditions: IF Flowise chatflow outputs contain secrets or sensitive inputs
IF Gemini CLI is pointed at the same filesystem tree or copied artifacts
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Rotate or redact credentials before passing files between agents
Run each agent in a separate workspace
Restrict outbound network access for one agent during handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has write_filesystem and shared state via server datastore; Gemini CLI has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared state via filesystem and git only. In a shared repo or workspace, both can mutate the same files and git state without any locking mechanism shown in the profiles, so concurrent writes can corrupt work or overwrite each other.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF writes occur concurrently or without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent while the other writes git state
Use a lock file around shared edits
Review and merge changes manually before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder whose outputs can become downstream inputs, while Gemini CLI can act on files and shell commands. If Gemini CLI consumes Flowise-produced artifacts without verification, mistaken or malicious content can cascade into code changes, file edits, or other actions. The profiles do not show a default verification barrier.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses Flowise-generated text, plans, or files as authoritative input
IF Gemini CLI then executes shell or file actions based on that input
mitigations: Require human review of Flowise outputs before Gemini CLI acts
Add a validation step that checks Flowise artifacts against source data
Limit Gemini CLI to read-only mode for the handoff
Use explicit schemas for exchanged messages
requires-engineering: implement signed or hashed handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and tool credentials, while Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment. If regulated data or secrets are placed into shared workspaces, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches through logs, files, or API calls. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in either agent
IF logs or retained files are shared across the two workspaces
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Delete temporary artifacts after each run
Review logging settings for both agents
Separate environments by data class
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
